subject: general
question: What was the poverty rate in India in 2019-21, according to the India National Multidimensional Poverty Index, 2023?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**14.96%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2023** was developed to measure poverty comprehensively, going beyond income-based measures.
 
• According to the MPI 2023, the poverty rate in India for the period 2019-21 was **0.1496**, representing a significant milestone in the country's efforts to alleviate poverty.
 
• The index uses three broad dimensions—**Health**, **Education**, and **Living Standards**—each with specific indicators to evaluate multidimensional poverty.
 
• The **Health dimension** includes indicators such as **nutrition, child mortality, and maternal health**.
 
• For the **Education dimension**, indicators like **years of schooling** and **school attendance** are considered.
 
• The **Living Standards dimension** covers areas such as **electricity access, drinking water, sanitation, housing, cooking fuel, and asset ownership**.
 
• The reduction in poverty, as indicated by the MPI 2023, highlights **India's progress in improving living conditions**, particularly in rural areas.
 
• This report aligns with the goals of the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 1, which aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere.
 
• The methodology of the MPI was developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• The poverty reduction achievements are attributed to several **government schemes** such as **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, **Ujjwala Yojana**, **Swachh Bharat Mission**, and rural employment programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India National Multidimensional Poverty Index**__

 __
 
• The MPI measures **poverty** based on a **set of deprivations** that households face in their daily lives.
 
• The MPI framework is considered more comprehensive than traditional income-based measures of poverty.
 
• This index is particularly important for targeting **policy interventions** and addressing the multifaceted challenges of poverty.
 
• The MPI is also used to **monitor progress** toward achieving the SDGs, especially in developing nations.
 
 
 
• **Government Schemes Contributing to Poverty Reduction**__
 __
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY):** Focuses on providing affordable housing to the urban and rural poor.
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission:** Aims to improve sanitation and eliminate open defecation.
 
• **Ujjwala Yojana:** Promotes the use of cleaner cooking fuel by providing subsidized LPG connections to poor households.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):** Ensures employment opportunities in rural areas to enhance livelihood security.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of MPI for Policy**__
 
 
• The MPI helps governments identify **specific areas of deprivation** that require immediate attention.
 
• It offers valuable insights into the **effectiveness of policies** aimed at poverty alleviation.
 
• The index also promotes **comparative analysis** between different regions and demographic groups within a country.
